verdicts.why: Hela never tries to claim Asgard; the threat is the Hulk smashing toward the palace where Odin lies in the Odinsleep, which Thor says would bring Ragnarok. Hela only claims Bruce Banner's soul.
Tony is not framed: Fury holds him on the Helicarrier as the only surviving witness, Tony breaks out, and Fury then calls him a fugitive. The fix just drops 'framed'.

At the end of the Agent Carter One-Shot, Howard Stark says Carter will run S.H.I.E.L.D. with him, so 'The Strategic Scientific Reserve' is out of date from that title. Captain Marvel uses S.H.I.E.L.D. throughout, and the full name is first spelled out by Coulson in Iron Man ('That's quite a mouthful'), so stage 1 stays at Iron Man.

Valentina presents the team to the press as the New Avengers to save herself. Fourteen months later the team is arguing over Sam Wilson's lawsuit about their use of the Avengers trademark, so nothing shows she owns the name.

value: S.H.I.E.L.D.: Strategic Homeland Intervention, Enforcement and Logistics Division
verdicts.why: Under the on-screen-name rule, the name S.H.I.E.L.D. is said at the end of the Agent Carter One-Shot and the full name is first spoken in Iron Man. So add a short-name stage at the One-Shot and keep the full-name stage at Iron Man. This is the same fix as item 2.

value: Active. Fisk free again, back running crime
Grieving Foggy. Building a resistance against Mayor Fisk
verdicts.why: Status means real status. In Hawkeye, Fisk is out of prison and running the Tracksuit Mafia, and in Echo he is recovering from Maya's shot and still offering her his empire. So 'Fisk in prison' is false from Hawkeye until Born Again S1, and the reveal belongs to Hawkeye.
WHIH Newsfront's Everhart interviews Scott Lang by video from San Quentin as a soon-to-be-released prisoner, not someone already released.
